paragraphs.text: Nearly three hundred crowns, dominions, clans and island lordships divide Aoaz, and a handful of them are great powers. Each great power leads a league of lesser crowns, and most have a rival whom they watch more closely than any other neighbour.

Aenor, the Middle Kingdom, rules from Parim and leads the Middle Kingdom Concord, and its rivals are Lerendor and Zol. Lerendor rules from Sonargur and leads the Leren Compact with Eekedor. Coldor rules the frozen interior and western ports of the Cold Lands from Fandanar and leads the Northern Accord with Horidor, and Isengard is its rival.

In the East Lands, Noris rules from Furvior and holds the Noris Treaty with Gondolin, and Stabilo rules from Postondoroth and holds the Stabilo Pact with Drak; each is the other’s rival on the southern trade roads. In the Dark Lands, Goldoroth rules from Cocanoor and is rival to Dondor, which rules from Notbuton and leads the Dark Sea Accord with Belonton.

In the south the ancient Great Spirit Volgan rules the Ember Lands from Nafeher and leads the Southern Dominion of Demon, Dolon and Nezer, and Mirolon is his rival. The black north and the islands of the Kusmeel belong to Zol, the Old God of Death, whose seat is Furviatlon. Zol has no bodily form and no crown of men among his allies, but he does not lack servants, and the most loyal of them is the Great Spirit Kusven.
paragraphs.note: Zol’s bodiless rule, his servants and Kusven are established; the seats and leagues are the working table.

paragraphs.text: The terms on which these leagues were first sworn are not written in the histories of Parim and Selen. Some realms stand in no league at all: Bordon, Dreson, Dulundur and the Troll Forest keep their own counsel, and Hirolon of the giants treats with Aenor as a sovereign kingdom.
paragraphs.note: Hirolon’s sovereignty is established; the leagues and the separate realms are the working table.

plate.subject: dominion banners around a throne hall

paragraphs.text: Aenor, the Middle Kingdom, is the central great power of Aoaz. From Parim it rules the plains, forests, mountains and Great Lake of the Middle Lands, and Aenor Isle with Asgard lies off its west coast. Aen founded it by uniting the kingdoms of men after the War of Men, and his victory began Year 1 of the First Age. The scholars do not agree whether the kingdom takes its name from Aen.

Aenor leads the Middle Kingdom Concord of twenty-six chartered dominions, among them Selen, Kilinti, Kingson, Konori, Hunhun, Asgard and Herez. Under the Charters of Parim each keeps its own lords and laws. Selen has its rangers, Kilinti its ents and forest peoples and Hunhun its riders, while Kingson lies behind the Great Wall and Herez on the southern marches. In war they owe a common army, and in peace they share free roads.
paragraphs.note: The dominions’ names and peoples and the twenty-six satellites are established working facts; the Charters and the Concord’s terms are proposed.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: The Cursed Lands and the Bloody Forest resist the crown, and Hirolon, the sovereign kingdom of the giants, treats with Aenor from outside the Charters. Whether each dominion is a member of the kingdom or a realm allied to it, the lawyers of Parim have argued for centuries without agreeing.

Aenor fell to Elzon at the end of the Second Age and was ruled by him through the Third. Restored at his death, it grew through the Fourth Age until it was as formidable as it had ever been, and in 4A 1748 it is rich, crowded and sure of its blessings.

sources.section: The Third Age and restored monarchy
Prologue: the peace that followed Elzon

paragraphs.text: In Parim the Golden Court means two things. It is the palace district of gilded halls that the Golden King completed in 4A 1733, where offices, titles and charters are bought, and it is the King’s party: the office-buyers, courtiers and merchant houses who profit from his extravagance.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: Its members are loyal to the King because the King is profitable. They pay for their offices and recover the price from the offices, they flatter him and are favoured, and the dominions whose taxes pay for the gilding grumble at them more loudly than at the King himself.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord
III. The Golden King and the empty throne

paragraphs.text: The old families of Parim who did not buy their places look on the Golden Court with contempt and do business with it every day.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

plate.subject: companies of the Lost Cause under a plain banner

paragraphs.text: In 4A 1741 the Golden King founded the Lost Cause, a league of the Concord and willing foreign crowns against “the powers of the dark”. He named himself its first lord and spent its first treasury on a triumph. It was formed to guard the kingdom against the return of dark powers such as Volgan, and it was formed just as much for the King’s prestige.
paragraphs.note: The Golden King founding the Lost Cause against the dark powers and for his prestige is established; the year, the league’s members and the triumph are proposed.

paragraphs.text: Its councils and alliances are real enough, but its founder uses it for his own glory, and his corruption has weakened trust in it. Most of Aoaz treats it as royal vanity against old legends. Its court branch is ceremonial, while its frontier companies, rangers and scholars are real and take it seriously, and some of its officers are genuine defenders of Aenor.
paragraphs.note: The founder’s misuse and its sincere officers are established; the court and frontier branches are proposed.

sources.section: III. The Golden King and the empty throne
The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: Its scholars hold that the old holy things of Aoaz must be kept from the dark, and above all the crystal that Horos guards in the Castle of Yeldenne, which they would see protected.
The Lost Cause outgrew its founder. Its companies and allied crowns became the shield of the Concord, and the dominions that had laughed at the King’s league stood behind it when the danger came.

The Lost Cause went over to the Man from the Ice. Its frontier companies and scholars, who had gathered proof of his ancestry, became his army, and the league that the Golden King founded for his own glory fought for another man’s cause.
paragraphs.note: Part of the Lost Cause supporting the heir is established; its frontier branches gathering proof are proposed.

entries.title: The Houses of the First Light
entries.subtitle: Fourth Age · Order

paragraphs.text: The Houses of the First Light began as refuges, hospitals and grain stores in the ruined towns of the Third Age, where their healers and scribes built on the medicine and farming of the Second Age. They are the relief houses of the Deliverer, and many of their people are sincere workers of charity.
In 4A 11 the Houses received royal charters to keep the grain stores, hospitals and birth rolls of the kingdom. Their physicians have taught at the universities of Parim and Selen since 4A 340.

Over the centuries the Houses became among the most trusted bodies of the restored kingdom. Their hand is in charity, schooling and the public records of every province, and there are few families in Aenor that they have not fed, nursed or written down.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: The Houses were Afrit’s from the beginning. They grew from the Houses of Refuge of the Second Age, where his hidden followers made each gift of grain, medicine or shelter into a small obligation that could pass from a family to a guild, a temple or a lord. Every sincere House that honoured the Deliverer was one more channel for his influence.

sources.section: Prologue: the peace that followed Elzon

paragraphs.text: By the Fourth Age the Houses could sway appointments, royal marriages, charity, records, schooling and taxes. Their rolls told the Hidden Council who lived where and who moved, and their grain stores told it who could be made grateful. Few of the healers ever knew whom they served.

About 4A 1520 a temple-state grew in the Zilin Hills of the Magical Lands around a hermitage of the Deliverer. The Worshipdom holds three valleys and almost no army. Its worth lies in the pilgrims, couriers and confessors who pass through it on their way to every court in Aoaz.

sources.section: III. The Kingdom Behind the Throne, 4A 1000 to 4A 1729

paragraphs.text: It is the one land of the Deliverer that answers to his priests alone. Kings send gifts to its hermitage, pilgrims climb to it from every region, and its couriers carry letters faster than most royal posts.

The Worshipdom is the visible hub of Afrit’s network. Afrit holds no clear dominion of his own, and his strength lies in the networks he keeps everywhere. The agents who pass through the Zilin Hills as pilgrims and couriers carry his orders out and bring the secrets of every court back.
paragraphs.note: Afrit having no clear dominion and networks everywhere is established; the Worshipdom as their hub is proposed.

paragraphs.text: Through the Fourth Age Afrit kept a council and many servants, agents, spies and networks. It influenced the kings of Aenor and in the end ruled much of their administration from behind the throne. Ordinary worshippers know him by the human name Aurevan, and only his inner council knows him as Afrit.
paragraphs.note: The council and its rule behind the kings are established; the name Aurevan is proposed.

paragraphs.text: The Council took its lasting form about 4A 1100, with four seats for royal administration, worship, foreign agents and the recovery of artifacts. It works through the temples, the relief houses, foreign envoys, gatherers of secrets and merchant connections. Its members, their titles and their quarrels are not known outside it.
paragraphs.note: The Council’s means are established; the four seats and the date are proposed.

sources.section: III. The Kingdom Behind the Throne, 4A 1000 to 4A 1729

paragraphs.text: Merovan, Keeper of the Seals, holds the seals of administration and is the member whom Afrit trusts to hold Aenor in his absence. The Golden King is one of the least capable kings the Council has ever managed.
paragraphs.note: A council member able to govern in Afrit’s absence and the Golden King as its weakest puppet are established; the name Merovan is proposed.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: Beyond Aenor the Council has worked for centuries to strengthen its hold in the East Lands and South Lands. Its eastern branch has courted their courts since about 4A 1300, so that Afrit has a reserve seat of power if Aenor is ever threatened.
paragraphs.note: The eastern and southern reserve is established; the date is proposed.

sources.section: II. Roka's necklace and the gathering of powers

paragraphs.text: No chronicle tells what became of the Hidden Council after Afrit’s death, nor of Merovan of the Seals, nor of the men in many courts who had served it.

plate.subject: demon banners at a desert fortress

paragraphs.text: Volgan, the ancient Great Spirit and principal dark lord of Aoaz, rules the Ember Lands south of the Middle Lands from Nafeher. His Southern Dominion takes in the demon realms of Demon, Dolon and Nezer, whose old name is Nazerun. His realm holds grave hosts, Netherborn demons, orcs, ogres, monster clans and necromantic orders.

About 4A 1650 Volgan’s strength returned. Demon, Dolon and Nezer swore to him and formed the Southern Dominion, and Mirolon fortified its passes. Mirolon, the human kingdom that Volgan conquered in the First Age, is free again and stands in his way.
paragraphs.note: Mirolon as Volgan’s rival is established; the date of the Dominion’s forming is proposed.

sources.section: III. The Kingdom Behind the Throne, 4A 1000 to 4A 1729

paragraphs.text: Volgan’s authority does not reach every monster of the Dark Lands or of the north, and he is no Old God, so his necromancy is not an authority over Death itself. In the far south of the Ember Lands lie the Nether, the seat of the King of Demons, and the Abyss, which are places of their own.
For a century Volgan has rebuilt his strength behind the storms and heat of the Ember Lands, and few outside Mirolon watch him.
Volgan’s manifested body was destroyed, and with it broke many of the bonds that held his hosts together. Whether his spirit survives is not known.

sources.section: Proposed continuity details, not yet confirmed

entries.title: The Treaty of the Narrow Strait
entries.subtitle: Fourth Age · Treaty

paragraphs.text: In 4A 512 the North Lands and Aenor signed the Treaty of the Narrow Strait and promised each other defence across the strait. It is the “old alliance” of the North, and under it the North Lands must defend Aenor in war.

Lerendor’s fleets guard the strait, and its kings are proud. Since the toll quarrel of 4A 1716 the Leren court has doubted the Treaty, and in Sonargur men argue whether to honour it, to break it, or to make it the means of Leren mastery over the strait.
Lerendor withdrew from the Treaty of the Narrow Strait. The old alliance of the North was ended, and Aenor faced its enemies without the Leren fleets at its side.

sources.section: V. The end of the age, 4A 1748 to 4A 1760

paragraphs.text: Lerendor honoured the Treaty of the Narrow Strait. When Aenor was attacked, the Leren crown went to its defence as its forefathers had sworn in 4A 512, and the old alliance of the North held.

The Golden King’s sudden death left Aenor with a succession that no ordinary claimant could settle. Four camps contended for the crown: the Golden Court, the Free Dominions, the Deliverer’s Faithful and the Stranger’s Host.

sources.section: III. The Golden King and the empty throne

paragraphs.text: The Golden Court was the late King’s party of office-buyers, courtiers and merchant houses, who wanted the gilded order to go on under a new head. The Free Dominions were the chartered dominions that wanted their liberties under the Charters of Parim and no master in Parim stronger than themselves.
paragraphs.note: The camps are established; their aims as described are proposed.

sources.section: The Middle Lands: Aenor and the Concord

paragraphs.text: The Deliverer’s Faithful held that the god who had kept the kingdom for centuries should keep it now, and the temples and much of the royal council stood with them. The Stranger’s Host was the people’s own camp of common folk, frontier soldiers and the poor of the dominions, who wanted a king that owed nothing to the court and whose hopes gathered around the stranger called the Man from the Ice.
paragraphs.note: The camps are established; the public labels the Deliverer’s Faithful and the Stranger’s Host and the camps’ make-up are proposed.

sources.section: III. The Golden King and the empty throne

paragraphs.text: The King’s death decided nothing between them. Which camp would prevail was not settled when he was buried, and the histories of Parim and Selen record the struggle as it went.

The Deliverer’s Faithful were Afrit’s supporters. Many of the priests and councillors who called for the god’s protection did so sincerely, but they were following the design of the Hidden Council, which had arranged the King’s death and the crisis that followed it.

sources.section: III. The Golden King and the empty throne

paragraphs.text: The Stranger’s Host was Eindil’s Host. The man whom the common folk followed as the Man from the Ice was Eindil, son of Ein, son of Aen, and the people’s camp was the camp of the old royal line.
